Penalties
Warning and progressive penalty

Point penalties and severe penalties

First offence: warning. Second: 5-point deduction. Subsequent offences: 10, 20, 30 points, and so on. The count resets at the start of each session, except for obstructive play, including deliberate delays.
Mahjong Competition Rules of the EMA, version of 20 June 2009.
Erroneous kong, pong, chow or hua call: the player calls but fails to perform the action, uses an incorrect term, or calls pong too late.
Revealing tiles before a kong, pong, chow or hua call: the call is invalid, and the revealed tiles must be discarded.
Calling and claiming a tile before exposing the matching tiles.
Claiming a false set, before discarding: it may be corrected, but the incorrectly exposed tiles must be discarded.
Replacing a false flower, before taking the replacement tile into the hand: it may be corrected, and the incorrectly exposed tiles must be discarded.
Drawing a tile from the wrong place in the wall: it may be corrected before putting the tile into the hand.
Revealing an opponent's tiles: subject to further penalty.
Prematurely destroying the wall or the discard area: subject to further penalty.
Passing information: subject to further penalty.
False hu without exposing tiles.
Erroneous hu call: calling something other than hu or mahjong, or exposing tiles before calling hu.
Failing to keep the winning hand intact: using hand tiles to count. Using flowers to count forfeits the flowers, but the hand remains valid.
Claiming a false set, after discarding: it cannot be undone.
Replacing a false flower after taking the replacement tile into the hand: it cannot be undone. The false flower remains on the table and counts as a discard for claiming hu or Last tile.
Drawing from the wrong place and putting the tile into the hand: dead hand only if an opponent points it out immediately.
Failing to take a claimed tile before the next two players have discarded.
False hu by player A when player B exposed tiles: A receives the applicable penalty. B has a dead hand and must discard the exposed tiles.
Too few or too many tiles.
False hu, fewer than 8 points: dead hand and 10 points to each opponent.
False hu with an invalid hand structure: not four sets and a pair (or another accepted structure), a false set, or a wrong tile count. Dead hand and 20 points to each opponent.
Forgetting to take the winning tile: 10 points deducted. The hand remains valid and is scored as usual.
Late by 10 minutes or less: 10 points deducted.
Late by 11 to 15 minutes: 20 points deducted.
Late by more than 15 minutes: the player forfeits the current session and scores 0 table points. A substitute plays the session.
Obstructive play: delaying the game, or seriously revealing tiles or information. The referee may impose 10 to 60 points and/or a dead hand.
Serious disruption: cheating or obstructing the competition, including repeated delaying. Immediate disqualification.
